rejected.title: Consumer rewards
card: Loyalty program
a scheme where a business gives points, discounts or free items to customers who keep buying from it.
Interest
money a bank or other financial institution pays you for keeping your savings with it.
Investment return
money gained from something you put money into, such as shares. Returns can be higher than interest, but they are not guaranteed and may be a loss.
Loyalty programs also have a cost. Businesses use them to collect data on what you buy, and the rewards can encourage you to spend more than you planned.
rejected.remember: Rewards pay people for saving, investing or staying loyal, and loyalty schemes also gather data and nudge spending.

a.q: Which is a way that a loyalty program benefits the business that runs it?
opts: It records what customers buy
It pays customers interest on savings
It guarantees customers a return
It stops customers spending too much
a.why: Loyalty programs collect data on what customers buy, which the business can use to plan offers. Paying interest is what a bank does for savings, not what a loyalty program does.
a.clue: Think about what the business learns about each member.

b.q: Priya joins a bookshop's loyalty program and gets a free book after ten purchases. She now buys books she did not plan to get so she can reach ten sooner. Which idea does this best show?
opts: The reward led her to spend more than planned
The reward earned her interest on her savings
The reward gave her a guaranteed return
The reward stopped the shop collecting her data
b.why: Priya spends more than she planned in order to earn the free book, so the program has encouraged her spending. A free book is not interest, which a bank pays on savings, and it is not an investment return. Loyalty programs collect data rather than stop it.
b.clue: Ask why Priya bought books she had not planned to buy.
